terms.gloss: an attempt, an undertaking; an effort
evidence: Verg. A. 12.910–911: in mediīs cōnātibus aegrī succidimus
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “an attempt, effort, undertaking, enterprise, endeavor”; in the plural, efforts: multīs frūstrā cōnātibus captīs, after many vain attempts (Liv. 3.5.6, Lewis & Short). The verb is cōnārī (see try).

terms.gloss: an attempt; usually plural, cōnāta, what one has set out to do
evidence: Caes. BG 1.3.6: perfacile factū esse illīs probat cōnāta perficere

phrases.latin: sī perrumpere possent cōnātī, operis mūnītiōne et mīlitum concursū et tēlīs repulsī, hōc cōnātū dēstitērunt
phrases.english: they tried to see if they could break through, but were driven back by the earthworks, the soldiers’ charge and missiles, and gave up the attempt

phrases.latin: ac velut in somnīs, oculōs ubi languida pressit nocte quiēs, nēquīquam avidōs extendere cursūs velle vidēmur et in mediīs cōnātibus aegrī succidimus
phrases.english: and as in dreams, when at night drowsy rest has closed our eyes, we seem to want, in vain, to run on eagerly, and in the middle of our efforts we sink down, exhausted

sources: Lewis & Short: conatus · Lewis & Short: conatum
